choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) voice — (B) narrows — (C) dominate
(A) voice — (B) widens — (C) avoid
(A) voice — (B) widens — (C) dominate
(A) conceal — (B) narrows — (C) avoid
(A) conceal — (B) widens — (C) dominate
choice.ex: (A) voice (B) widens (C) dominate 근거 ❸❹ 해설: (A) ❸ 대중적이라고 인식하는 사람들은 express them = 표명 / (B) ❹ occurs in a spiral — 한쪽은 상당한 주목, 다른 쪽은 거의 없음 = 격차가 넓어짐 / (C) ❹ 한쪽이 considerable publicity를 얻고 다른 쪽은 very little = 논의를 지배. conceal은 ❸ express와 반대, narrows는 ❹ 나선형 확대 와 반대, avoid는 주목을 독차지한다는 ❹와 반대. 요약문 해석: Noelle-Neumann에 따르면, 자신의 견해가 널리 받아들여진다고 믿는 사람들은 그것을 (A) 표명하는 경향이 있는 반면, 자신이 소수라고 생 각하는 사람들은 침묵을 지킨다. 이 양상이 반복되면서 두 진영 사이의 격차는 (B) 넓어지고, 마침내 한 입장이 공적 논의를 (C) 지배하게 되는 반면 다른 입장은 거의 사라진다.
choice.psg: ❶ As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. ❷ Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. ❸ The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet. ❹ This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. ❺ In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. ❻ According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions.
choice.body: According to Noelle-Neumann, people who believe their views are widely held tend to (A)________ them, while those who think they are in the minority keep silent. As this pattern repeats, the gap between the two sides (B)________, until one position comes to (C)________ public discussion while the other nearly disappears.

choice.ex: (A) suppressed (B) endorsed (C) isolated 근거 ❶❺❻ 해설: (A) ❶ muted their opinions ~ perceived to be unpopular = 억누름 / (B) ❻ perceive that others share their opinions = 다른 사람들에게 지 지받는 / (C) ❸ 대중적이라고 생각하지 않는 사람들 remain quiet = 고립감을 느끼는 쪽이 침묵. broadcast(널리 알렸다)는 ❶ muted와 반대, rejected 는 ❻과 반대, supported라고 느끼는 사람은 오히려 의견을 드러내므로(❸❻) 침묵하는 쪽이 될 수 없음. 요약문 해석: Noelle-Neumann은 선거 기간 동안 사람들이 자신의 의견이 인기 없어 보일 때 흔히 그 의견을 (A) 억누른다는 것을 알아차렸다. 그녀의 이 론에 따르면, 사람들은 자신의 입장이 다른 사람들에게 (B) 지지받는다고 느낄 때 대화, 배지, 범퍼 스티커, 소셜 미디어 게시물을 통해 더 선뜻 견해를 드 러내는 반면, (C) 고립되었다고 느끼는 사람들은 자신의 견해를 혼자 간직하는 경향이 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. ❷ Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. ❸ The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet. ❹ This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. ❺ In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. ❻ According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions.
choice.body: Noelle-Neumann noticed that during elections, people often (A)________ their opinions when those opinions seemed unpopular. Her theory holds that people display their views—through talk, buttons, bumper stickers, or social media posts—more readily when they feel their position is (B)________ by others, whereas those who feel (C)________ tend to keep their views to themselves.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.

Believing that one’s opinion is unpopular can discourage a person from discussing it with others.
The writer implies that putting a sticker on one’s car is one way of making a personal opinion public.
A view may seem less widespread than it really is because many of its supporters choose not to speak up.
The writer suggests that people who stay silent usually change their beliefs to match the majority view.
choice.ex: 원문은 사람들이 의견을 ‘표현하지 않는다(muted, remain quiet)’고만 할 뿐, 신념 자체를 다수에 맞춰 바꾼다는 언급은 없음(원문 밖 인과·과장). 나머지는 ❸❹ 침묵하는 쪽은 주목을 거의 못 받음 / ❺ bumper stickers on their cars / ❶❸ 인기 없다고 인식되면 침묵 / ❶❷ 관찰한 현상을 침묵의 나선이라 부름에서 추론 가능. ① 근거 ❶❷ — 선거 운동에 대한 Noelle-Neumann의 관찰은 그녀가 자신이 알아차린 양상에 이름을 붙이도록 이끌었다. ② 근거 ❶❸ — 자신의 의견이 인기 없다고 믿는 것은 사람이 그것을 다른 사람들과 논의하지 못하게 할 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❺ — 필자는 자기 차에 스티커를 붙이는 것이 개인적 의견을 공개하는 한 방법이라고 암시한다. ④ 근거 ❸❹ — 어떤 견해는 그 지지자 중 다수가 목소리를 내지 않기로 하기 때문에 실제보다 덜 퍼져 있는 것처럼 보일 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 필자는 침묵하는 사람들이 대개 다수의 견해에 맞추어 자신의 신념을 바꾼다고 시사한다.
choice.psg: ❶ As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. ❷ Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. ❸ The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet. ❹ This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. ❺ In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. ❻ According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: a tactic politicians use to avoid answering difficult questions from voters
a self-reinforcing cycle in which people who sense their view is unpopular stop speaking, making that view seem even weaker
a gradual drop in the number of citizens who bother to vote in elections
a quiet period of reflection that people need before forming their political opinions
a growing tendency for every group to express its views more and more loudly
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: Noelle-Neumann은 이것을 ‘침묵의 나선’이라고 부른다. 해설: '나선(spiral)'은 한 번의 침묵이 다음 침묵을 낳으며 점점 커지는 순환을 뜻함 — ❶ 인기 없다고 여겨지면 침묵 → ❸ 대중적이라 느끼는 쪽만 표현 → (❹) 한쪽은 주목, 다른 쪽은 거의 없음. ②는 silence의 문자적 의미(조용한 숙고) 함정 ③ 투표율은 원문에 없음(무관) ④ 정치인의 전략이 아니라 일반 사람들의 의견 표현 현상 ⑤ 모두가 크게 말한다는 것은 침묵과 정반대. ① 정치인들이 유권자의 어려운 질문에 대한 답을 피하기 위해 쓰는 전략 ② 자신의 견해가 인기 없다고 느끼는 사람들이 말을 멈추고, 그로 인해 그 견해가 훨씬 더 약해 보이게 되는 스스로 강화되는 순환 ③ 굳이 선거에서 투표하려는 시민 수의 점진적 감소 ④ 사람들이 정치적 의견을 형성하기 전에 필요한 조용한 숙고의 시간 ⑤ 모든 집단이 자신의 견해를 점점 더 크게 표현하는 증가하는 경향
choice.body: As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) altered — (B) superior — (C) practical
(A) unchanged — (B) superior — (C) practical
(A) unchanged — (B) superior — (C) traditional
(A) unchanged — (B) equivalent — (C) practical
(A) altered — (B) equivalent — (C) traditional
choice.ex: (A) unchanged (B) superior (C) practical 근거 ❷❸❺ 해설: (A) ❷ the physics wil be the same / ❺ nothing in the physics changes = 변하지 않는 / (B) ❸ physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other = 어느 단위도 우월하지 않음 / (C) ❸ for reasons of convenience = 실용적인(편리한). altered는 ❷❺와 반대, equivalent를 넣으면 ‘어떤 단위도 다른 단위와 동등하지 않다’가 되어 ❸과 반대, traditional(전통적인)은 선택 기준이 ‘편의’라는 ❸과 다름. 요약문 해석: 물리학자들은 다양한 단위와 척도로 거리와 온도를 서술하지만, 어느 것을 쓰든 물리적 원리 자체는 (A) 변하지 않는다. 따라서 어떤 단위도 다른 단위보다 (B) 우월하지 않으며, 우리는 그저 우리의 목적에 가장 (C) 실용적인 것을 고르면 된다.
choice.psg: ❶ Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. ❷ Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. ❸ We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. ❹ We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. ❺ Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. ❻ We conclude that the choice of scale is an arbitrary choice in description, and that any feature that depends on that choice is scale-dependent.
choice.body: Physicists describe distances and temperatures with various units and scales, but the physics itself stays (A)________ no matter which one is used. Therefore, no unit is (B)________ to another, and we may simply pick the one that is most (C)________ for our purposes.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) within — (B) convention — (C) inherent
(A) within — (B) discovery — (C) artificial
(A) outside — (B) discovery — (C) inherent
(A) outside — (B) convention — (C) inherent
(A) outside — (B) convention — (C) artificial
choice.ex: (A) outside (B) convention (C) inherent 근거 ❹❻ 해설: (A) ❹ is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit = 단위 밖에서는 존재하지 않음 / (B) ❻ an arbitrary choice in description = 우리의 관행(약속) / (C) ❹ 세상 어딘가에 존재하는 것이 아님 = 세계의 고유한 속성이 아님. within은 ‘단위 안에서는 존재하지 않는다’가 되어 뜻이 거꾸 로, discovery(발견)는 ❻ ‘임의적 선택’과 반대(자연에 있는 것을 찾아낸다는 뜻), artificial을 넣으면 ‘인위적 속성이 아니라’가 되어 결론과 정반대. 요약문 해석: 우리가 거리에 부여하는 특정한 수치는 우리가 고른 단위 (A) 밖에서는 존재하지 않는다. 마찬가지로, 온도 척도에 달려 있는 어떤 특성이든 물리적 세계의 (C) 고유한 속성이 아니라 우리의 (B) 관행(약속)의 산물이다.
choice.psg: ❶ Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. ❷ Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. ❸ We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. ❹ We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. ❺ Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. ❻ We conclude that the choice of scale is an arbitrary choice in description, and that any feature that depends on that choice is scale-dependent.
choice.body: The specific number we assign to a distance has no existence (A)________ the unit we have selected. In the same way, any feature that hinges on a temperature scale is a product of our (B)________ rather than an (C)________ property of the physical world.

choice.ex: 원문은 화씨·섭씨·켈빈 중 어느 것을 써도 물리적 원리가 변하지 않으며(❺) 척도 선택은 임의적(❻)이라고 할 뿐, 특정 척도가 더 정확 하다거나 채택해야 한다는 말은 없음(원문 밖 가치 판단 + ❸ 선호 없음과 충돌). ① ❷ feet or meters ~ the physics will be the same + ❸ 선호 없음 / ② ❹ 수치는 단위 선택에 따른 특성 / ③ ❺ likewise = 길이와 같은 사례 / ④ ❷❺ 단위·척도를 바꿔도 물리는 동일. ① 근거 없음(정답) — 과학자들은 켈빈 척도가 다른 척도들보다 온도를 더 정확하게 서술하므로 그것을 채택해야 한다. ② 근거 ❷❺ — 물리학자는 같은 현상을 다른 척도로 서술하고도 여전히 같은 물리적 결과에 도달할 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❷❸ — 피트와 미터는 물리학에서 공간적 거리를 표현하는 똑같이 받아들일 만한 방법이다. ④ 근거 ❹ — 거리에 대해 우리가 얻는 수치는 한 단위에서 다른 단위로 바꿀 때 달라진다. ⑤ 근거 ❺ — 필자는 온도 척도와 길이 단위를 비슷한 사례로 다룬다.

is a real property of nature that every unit must measure in exactly the same way

choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 우리는 더 나아가 두 지점 사이의 공간적 분리에 부여된 특정한 수치적 값과 같이 그 선택에 따른 어떠한 특성도 단위의 선택 과 동떨어져 세상 어딘가에 존재하는 것이 아니라고 결론짓는다. 해설: ‘세상 저 밖에 있지 않다’는 것은 그 수치가 자연 자체가 가진 객관적 특성이 아니라, 우리가 어떤 단위를 쓰기로 했느냐에 따라 생긴 서술의 산물이라 는 뜻 — 바로 뒤 'apart from a choice of unit'과 ❻의 결론이 뒷받침. 지구 표면에서 보이지 않는다는 선지는 out there의 문자적(공간적) 해석 함정, 자 연의 실제 속성이라는 선지는 정반대, 계산·실험에 쓸모없다는 선지는 ‘객관적 실재가 아님’을 ‘쓸모없음’으로 과장한 왜곡, 기록 실패 이야기는 원문과 무 관. ① 과학자들이 그것을 제대로 기록하지 못해서 오래전에 사라졌다 ② 모든 단위가 정확히 같은 방식으로 측정해야 하는 자연의 실제 속성이다 ③ 과학적 계산이나 실험에서 전혀 쓸모가 없다 ④ 너무 작아서 지구 표면 어디에서도 보일 수 없다 ⑤ 우리가 그것을 서술하기로 정한 방식과 별개로 자연의 객관적 사실로 존재하지 않는다

para.en: As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet. This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions.

Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. We conclude that the choice of scale is an arbitrary choice in description, and that any feature that depends on that choice is scale-dependent.

Even though sea creatures live in it, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to get rid of any extra salt it might bring with it. Salt absorbs water like a sponge. If you put a tiny mountain of salt on a small plate, then add enough water to the side, making sure an edge touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water. Now you have a pile of wet salt. Notice that it has increased in size. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If the body fluids in a sea animal are saltier than the seawater it lives in, then the extra salt in the creature’s body will absorb seawater. This can cause them to swell up. On the other hand, if the amount of salt in the seawater is higher than the amount of salt in the body fluids of a sea animal, the extra salt in the water will draw fluids out of the creature’s body, causing it to dehydrate and shrink.

Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small club-shaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore- and hindwings, a feature only present in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies are simply wrong. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey. It’s more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects.

There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: active management and inactive management. Active management does something to the population ― such as increasing or decreasing its size ― in a direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, respectively. Populations can also be actively managed by altering the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population. If population numbers are too low for the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated, such as predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement to provide required cover for neonates from predators. These efforts represent active approaches to management. Other populations may not be actively managed, like those in national parks. In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, which often involves management of humans and not animals.
